module.purpose: This module provides a higher-order server-side rendering wrapper that exposes a Content Security Policy nonce through page props.
module.summary: The module defines a generic prop type and an asynchronous wrapper around Next.js server-side property loaders. The wrapper preserves redirects and other non-props responses, obtains a nonce from the request and response, records whether nonce generation succeeded through an HTTP response header, and merges the nonce into returned props only when available.
module.businessContext: This supports nonce-based Content Security Policy protection for scripts rendered by web pages. Failure can prevent page components from receiving a usable nonce or obscure CSP setup problems during debugging.
classes: WithNonceProps (~L5-7): Extends server-rendered page props with an optional CSP nonce
functions: withNonce (~L13-42): Wraps server-side props loading to attach CSP nonce metadata
systemCapabilities: Report nonce availability through response headers

io: Sets the x-csp HTTP response header to ssr or false.
mutationOfArg: Mutates context.res by setting the x-csp response header.

edgeCases.inputShape: Server-side response without a props property
edgeCases.behavior: Returns the response immediately without generating a nonce or setting the x-csp header.

edgeCases.inputShape: Props response with a falsy or unavailable nonce
edgeCases.behavior: Uses null for nonce props, sets x-csp to false, and leaves the nonce property absent.

edgeCases.inputShape: Props response with a truthy nonce
edgeCases.behavior: Adds the nonce to props and sets x-csp to ssr.

invariants.description: A server response without a props property is returned unchanged.
Nonce is added to returned props only when its value is truthy.
Props responses always receive an x-csp header indicating nonce availability.
The CSP status header is set before the enriched response is returned.

assumptions.description: The supplied loader conforms to Next.js GetServerSideProps and accepts the provided context.
The server-side response shape uses a props property to identify renderable page data.
context.res provides a setHeader method compatible with Node.js HTTP responses.

ambiguities.question: What exact nonce-generation and failure behavior does csp provide?

concurrencyModel.notes: Each invocation awaits its supplied loader and uses request-local context; no shared mutable state is maintained by this module.

moduleContractTests.scenario: The wrapped server-side props function returns a redirect or not-found response without props.
moduleContractTests.then: the returned response is the same non-props response and csp is not invoked
moduleContractTests.rationale: Preserves Next.js redirect and not-found responses without attempting to add serialized props.

moduleContractTests.scenario: The wrapped server-side props function returns props and CSP provides a nonce.
moduleContractTests.then: the result props contain value: 1 and nonce: "abc", and context.res.setHeader was called with "x-csp" and "ssr"
moduleContractTests.rationale: Pins nonce propagation and the success diagnostic header.

moduleContractTests.scenario: The wrapped server-side props function returns props but CSP does not provide a nonce.
moduleContractTests.then: the result props contain value: 1 without a nonce property, and context.res.setHeader was called with "x-csp" and "false"
moduleContractTests.rationale: Guards serializability by omitting unavailable nonce values.
